t.1.5.6: O brahmin, O great sage, I shall recount to you this lineage of the Bhārgavas, joined with tales and grounded in the lore of the Purāṇa.
t.1.5.7: Bhṛgu's dearly beloved son was the Bhārgava named Cyavana; Cyavana's heir, in turn, was the righteous one named Pramati. And to Pramati, too, a son was born by Ghṛtācī, called Ruru.
t.1.5.8: From Ruru too, your forefather, a son was born in Pramadvarā: Śunaka, righteous-souled and a master of the Vedas.
t.1.5.9: He was an ascetic, renowned, learned in the sacred tradition and the foremost among the knowers of brahman; most righteous and truthful in speech, he was disciplined, with his senses held in check.
t.1.5.5: O delight of the Bhṛgus, hear first what was studied by my father and then thoroughly by me as well: the excellent lineage of the Bhṛgus, which is honored by the gods together with Indra, Agni and the hosts of Maruts.
t.1.5.4: The Sūta said: O best of the twice-born, that which was thoroughly studied of old by the great-souled brahmins headed by Vaiśampāyana, and which was also recited by them in former times.
t.1.5.11: Bhṛgu's dearly beloved wife was renowned by the name Pulomā. In her there arose an embryo, sprung from the seed of Bhṛgu.
t.1.5.10: Śaunaka said: O son of a sūta, tell me, since I am asking, how that great-souled Bhārgava came to be renowned by the name Cyavana.
t.1.5.13: When Bhṛgu, the best of those who uphold dharma, had gone out for his ritual bath, the Rākṣasa Puloman then came to his hermitage.
t.1.5.12: Then, O scion of Bhṛgu, when in due time that embryo had been conceived in Pulomā, the lawful wife of the glorious one, a woman whose conduct matched his own...
t.1.5.14: Having entered that hermitage and seen the blameless wife of Bhṛgu, he was overcome by desire and lost his senses.
t.1.5.15: Then lovely-looking Pulomā invited that Rākṣasa, who had arrived as a guest, to partake of forest fare such as fruits and roots.
t.1.5.3: Therein I wish to hear of the ancient Bhārgava lineage. Tell this tale, for we are ready to listen to you.
t.1.5.16: Then, O brahmin, the Rākṣasa, tormented by love, seeing her there, became delighted, wishing to carry off that blameless woman.
t.1.5.17: Then, in the fire-sanctuary, he saw Jātavedas blazing; and the Rākṣasa then questioned him, Pāvaka, the blazing fire.
t.1.5.18: Tell me, Agni, whose wife is she? You are asked in the name of truth. You are truthful, Pāvaka, so speak the truth to me who asks you.
t.1.5.19: For this fair-complexioned woman was first chosen by me to be my wife; but afterward her father gave her to Bhṛgu, who acted falsely.
t.1.5.20: If this woman of beautiful hips, met here in solitude, is the wife of Bhṛgu, then tell me the truth, for I wish to carry her away from the hermitage.
t.1.5.21: For wrath stands today as if burning up my heart, because Bhṛgu has taken this slender-waisted woman, who was first my wife.
t.1.5.2: For in the Purāṇa divine stories are told, and the earliest lineages of the wise; these we heard long ago, first from your father.
t.1.5.23: O Agni, you move always within all beings, like a witness to their good and evil deeds; O wise one, speak a truthful word.
t.1.5.22: Having thus addressed the blazing Jātavedas, that Rakṣas, suspicious about Bhṛgu's wife, questioned him again and again.
t.1.5.1: Śaunaka said: Long ago, my dear, your father studied the entire Purāṇa. Have you too, O son of Lomaharṣaṇa, studied all of it?
t.1.5.24: She who was formerly my wife was carried off by Bhṛgu, a doer of falsehood. If this is indeed she, you ought to tell me the truth.
t.1.5.26: Hearing those words of his, the seven-flamed Agni was deeply distressed; afraid both of falsehood and of Bhṛgu's curse, he spoke softly thus.
t.1.5.25: Once I have heard it from you, O Jātavedas, I shall carry off Bhṛgu's wife from the hermitage while you look on; speak a true word to me.
